r29_boundary_coverage.reason: In this stochastic replay the executor opened Show roots before proposing the first bottom Move commit, so the r28 failure boundary did not recur.
r29_boundary_coverage.deterministic_contract_coverage: Unit tests prove that only an accessibility-bound top-left Show roots tap can execute when the r29 marker is present; press_back and other targets execute zero actions.

bounded_repair_candidate.reason: The same wait had already been used twice without changing the semantic state.

root_cause.summary: After the single successful destination commit, later policy prompts did not carry the already-audited post-commit state, and the dedicated guard had only a generic repair directive.
details: The first Move commit was correctly bound to Ringtones and accepted by the consequential-action Critic.
The next screenshot returned to a stale source/search view, which the model misread as an instruction to start another move.
The post-commit guard correctly blocked all three later Move to candidates.
Its generic one-repair prompt permitted wait; two waits made no semantic progress, and the third identical repair conflicted with the active Critic constraint.

r30_required_change.scope: All policy steps after the first audited bottom Copy/Move commit, plus the bounded repair for a blocked repeat transfer.
mechanism: Expose only the already-audited boolean post_destination_commit_active in the policy prompt.
Forbid selecting the task item, reopening overflow Move/Copy, or waiting on an unchanged stale source/search view.
Direct the policy to use reversible navigation to inspect the requested destination or return terminal status only with direct-screen completion evidence.
When a repeat transfer is blocked, constrain the sole repair to exactly press_back so the menu or second picker is dismissed without another mutation.
prohibited: Using native evaluator reward inside the policy loop
Automatically declaring success after a commit
Changing task, seed, budgets, evaluator, or thresholds
